blocks.text: MOSES’ SPOKESMAN: "AARON THY BROTHER SHALL BE THY PROPHET" (EXODUS 7:1) · EXODUS & WILDERNESS
Aaron. Spoke the words the LORD gave Moses, to the elders of Israel and to Pharaoh.
Called, as three accounts tell it
“Is not Aaron the Levite thy brother? I know that he can speak well.”

The word came to Aaron through Moses: "thou shalt speak unto him, and put words in his mouth: and I will be with thy mouth, and with his mouth". "Aaron spake all the words which the LORD had spoken unto Moses". Exodus 4:15–16 Exodus 4:28–30

Scholars' viewKeil reads Exodus 4:16 and 7:1 together: "Aaron would stand in the same relation to Moses, as a prophet to God: the prophet only spoke what God inspired him with"; at 7:1 Aaron is "the prophet of Moses, as being the person who would announce to Pharaoh the revelations of Moses."[1][2]

From the textOur count in the KJV: the LORD speaks to Aaron alone in five places (Exodus 4:27; Leviticus 10:8; Numbers 18:1, 18:8, 18:20), and to Moses and Aaron together in 17 verses. Exodus 4:27 Leviticus 10:8 Numbers 18:1 Numbers 18:8 Numbers 18:20

As high priest he was to bear the breastplate of judgment, with "the Urim and the Thummim", upon his heart before the LORD, and Moses put them in the breastplate; later his son Eleazar was to ask counsel "after the judgment of Urim". Exodus 28:29–30 Leviticus 8:8 Numbers 27:21
From the textExodus 7:1 is the only verse that calls Aaron a prophet, and there he is the prophet of Moses. Exodus 7:1
KING OF EGYPT (NOT NAMED IN SCRIPTURE)
“Aaron thy brother shall speak unto Pharaoh, that he send the children of Israel out of his land.”
LEADER OF ISRAEL, LAWGIVER AND PROPHET
“Alas, my lord, I beseech thee, lay not the sin upon us, wherein we have done foolishly, and wherein we have sinned.”
The word in its main themes
“The God of the Hebrews hath met with us: let us go, we pray thee, three days’ journey into the desert, and sacrifice unto the LORD our God”
“The LORD bless thee, and keep thee: The LORD make his face shine upon thee, and be gracious unto thee: The LORD lift up his countenance upon thee, and give thee peace.”
“that ye may teach the children of Israel all the statutes which the LORD hath spoken unto them by the hand of Moses”
To whom the word was spoken
“And Aaron spake all the words which the LORD had spoken unto Moses, and did the signs in the sight of the people.”
TO THE PEOPLE, AT THE GOLDEN CALF
“To morrow is a feast to the LORD.”
“Hath the LORD indeed spoken only by Moses? hath he not spoken also by us?”
Between the dead and the living
Who stood with him, and against him

Because "ye rebelled against my word at the water of Meribah", Aaron was not to enter the land. On mount Hor Moses stripped him of his garments and put them on Eleazar, "and Aaron died there in the top of the mount"; Israel mourned him thirty days. Numbers 20:23–29
Numbers gives the date and age: he died "in the fortieth year" after the Exodus, "in the first day of the fifth month", aged 123. Numbers 33:38–39
Deuteronomy has a different place name: "to Mosera: there Aaron died, and there he was buried". Deuteronomy 10:6

Later Scripture remembers him as "Aaron whom he had chosen" and "Aaron the saint of the LORD", and Hebrews says no man takes the priestly honour "but he that is called of God, as was Aaron". Psalms 105:26 Psalms 106:16 Hebrews 5:4
Both: Mosera was the camp below mount Hor

Keil holds that the camp "is called Mosera in Deut. x. 6, and Moseroth" in Numbers 33, and lay in the Arabah near mount Hor, though "altogether unknown to us"; the camp took the mountain’s name because Aaron died and was buried there.[6]

Driver notes that Numbers 33 lists the stations in another order and has Aaron die on mount Hor "not at Moserah". He thinks the difference is due to "divergent traditions", and that the itinerary in Deuteronomy 10 is likely "not part of the original text" of the book. He calls Keil’s reconciliation possible but not probable.[22]

Scripture records no prophecy of the future given through Aaron; his recorded words as a speaker are the words given to Moses.
Exodus does not record any word of the LORD to Aaron about the calf; Deuteronomy 9:20 says the LORD "was very angry with Aaron" and that Moses prayed for him.
